requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

findings.claim: When no surrogate is supplied, the collector always calls CreateContractlessMembers and never inspects attributes on T. For example, if a referenced-assembly type has [MessagePackObject], [Key(42)] on Value, and [IgnoreMember] on Ignored, the generated user formatter still uses name-based string keys and serializes Ignored. This violates the explicit requirement that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile Project A containing a public [MessagePackObject] type with [Key(42)] Value and [IgnoreMember] Ignored into a metadata reference. In Project B, declare [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class MyObjectFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>. Run MessagePackGenerator and assert that the emitted formatter excludes Ignored and writes integer key 42; on head it instead contains Ignored and uses the contractless string-key template. The supplied receipt test MessagePackAttributesOnMetadataType_ControlKeysAndMembership demonstrates this.

hunches.claim: MessagePack attributes on T are ignored. When no surrogate is supplied, the collector always builds a contractless, string-keyed model from all public read-write members, without checking MessagePackObjectAttribute, KeyAttribute, or IgnoreMemberAttribute. Consequently, a referenced type carrying integer keys or ignored members gets a different wire contract, contrary to the explicit acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedMessagePackFormatterRequirementTests.HonorsMessagePackAttributesOnReferencedType. ProjectA.MyObject has [MessagePackObject], [Key(0)] and [Key(1)] members, and an [IgnoreMember] member. The test requires an array header of 2, no map header, and no generated serialization of the ignored member; the current contractless collector fails these assertions.

hunches.claim: When the formatted type already has MessagePack attributes, the new collector ignores them and always builds a contractless string-key model unless a surrogate is supplied. Consequently, the generated formatter for a [MessagePackObject] type with integer [Key] members writes a string-keyed map instead of the established integer-keyed array, contrary to the requirement that existing attributes be honored.

receipt_plan.detail: Define public class MyObject with [MessagePackObject] and one public read-write int property Value annotated [Key(0)]. With base-built code, serialize new MyObject { Value = 42 } using the ordinary generated formatter. With head-built code, add [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class MyObjectFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>; and serialize the same value with that formatter. Compare the bytes: the existing formatter should produce the integer-keyed array 0x91 0x2a, while this change's contractless path produces a string-keyed map for "Value".

hunches.claim: Formatters without a surrogate always use contractless member discovery, so existing [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember] attributes on T are ignored instead of honoured. An attributed external type with integer keys or ignored members will therefore be serialized with alphabetical string keys and all public read-write members, violating an explicit acceptance criterion.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an execution test for an external type marked [MessagePackObject] whose properties use non-sequential integer [Key] values and [IgnoreMember], with a formatter using only [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]. Serialize it and assert an array with the declared integer-key layout and omission of the ignored member; the current contractless branch produces a string-keyed map containing every public read-write member.

hunches.claim: The acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T are honoured has no test. Every execution-test T is explicitly attribute-free, so the suite would still pass if attributed types were always serialized with contractless member names and string keys.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator or execution test where T has [MessagePackObject] and integer [Key] annotations (or explicit string keys different from member names), without a surrogate; assert that the generated formatter uses those keys rather than contractless member names.

hunches.claim: No added test uses the required body-less declaration form. Both execution and diagnostic tests declare formatters with braces, so discovery or syntax handling that only works for body-bearing classes would go unnoticed.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Add the marker attribute with an optional SurrogateType property so Project B can supply MessagePack-specific keys and settings on a surrogate type mapped to T by property name. Code: In addition to basic formatter generation, the generator must resolve and validate the surrogate, read its MessagePack annotations, and apply them to T's corresponding properties; the attribute gains a public Type-valued SurrogateType surface.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add only the marker attribute and generate a bodyless partial formatter, using contractless public-member serialization by default and honoring DataContract or MessagePack metadata already present on T, without adding any new configuration mechanism. Code: The public API contains GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute without SurrogateType; key and union customization is limited to metadata already on T (including DataMember and related attributes), and user-defined attribute copies receive no special recognition.
